source_note: Every country cites its European Commission eInvoicing Country Factsheet (2026 edition). Countries whose mandates were provisional additionally cite the national legal source, which takes precedence where the factsheet lags — see notes for Norway, Slovenia and Spain in particular.

countries.name: Austria

phases.applies_to: All suppliers, including foreign ones, invoicing central government
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Central government requires supplier issuance via e-Rechnung.gv.at / USP; sub-central adoption is voluntary. Two national CIUS apply.

countries.name: Belgium

phases.applies_to: Public contracts of EUR 215,000 or more
Public contracts of EUR 30,000 or more
Public contracts below EUR 30,000 (contracts under EUR 3,000 exempt)
All VAT-registered businesses established in Belgium, for domestic transactions

countries.notes: Peppol is the exclusive route; an emailed PDF no longer satisfies the B2B obligation. Scope is VAT-registered businesses established in Belgium, including the small-business exemption scheme (turnover up to EUR 25,000); flat-rate farmers must at least be able to receive. Foreign businesses with a Belgian VAT number but no permanent establishment are not subject to the obligation (FPS Finance FAQ; the law is still being amended on this point). A tolerance period ran to 31 March 2026; since then fines of EUR 1,500, 3,000 and 5,000 apply for a first, second and further breach (Royal Decree of 8 July 2025). Structured e-reporting is planned from 1 January 2028. B2C is out of scope.

countries.name: Bulgaria

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, under Article 115a of the Public Procurement Act
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: A public consultation has been opened on adopting a mandatory clearance model along Italian/French lines; nothing adopted.

countries.name: Cyprus

phases.applies_to: Central public sector bodies
Sub-central entities
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Supplier issuance is voluntary. Mandatory B2B/B2C is a stated long-term objective with no timeline.

countries.name: Czechia

phases.applies_to: Public contracting authorities, under Act No. 134/2016 on Public Procurement
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: B2G runs through the NEN platform. ISDOC is the national format alongside EN 16931.

countries.name: Germany

phases.applies_to: All businesses established in Germany must be able to receive e-invoices (domestic B2B)
Issuers with prior-year total turnover above EUR 800,000 must issue e-invoices
All remaining issuers established in Germany (Kleinunternehmer, invoices up to EUR 250 and tickets exempt)

countries.notes: Legal basis is the Wachstumschancengesetz amending §14 UStG, with detail in the BMF circular of 15 October 2025. Scope is domestic B2B supplies where supplier and buyer are both established in Germany (seat, management or a fixed establishment involved in the supply); a foreign company with only a German VAT registration is not covered. The receive obligation has been universal since 2025 while issuance phases to 2028 — conflating the two is the most common error about the German mandate. In 2027 paper or PDF (with consent) remains allowed only for issuers whose prior-year total turnover was not more than EUR 800,000. Invoices from Kleinunternehmer (§ 19 UStG), invoices up to EUR 250 and tickets are permanently exempt from the issuing duty; Kleinunternehmer must still be able to receive.

countries.name: Denmark

phases.applies_to: All public contracting authorities (Bekendtgørelse nr. 346 af 15/03/2019)
No B2B e-invoicing mandate. The Bookkeeping Act requires the capability to send and receive structured invoices, not their use.

countries.notes: Frequently misreported as a B2B mandate. The 2022 Bookkeeping Act (bogføringsloven) mandates digital bookkeeping systems able to send and receive e-invoices (OIOUBL and PEPPOL BIS), but does not require invoices to be exchanged electronically. Companies that file annual reports (e.g. ApS, A/S) are covered whatever their turnover: from 1 July 2024 with a registered system, 1 January 2025 with other systems. Businesses that do not file annual reports (sole proprietorships, associations) are covered from 1 January 2026 if net turnover exceeded DKK 300,000 in two consecutive years. Using a system from the Erhvervsstyrelsen register is not mandatory. Suppliers to the public sector have sent e-invoices via NemHandel since 2005. OIOUBL 3.0 became mandatory 15 November 2025, with OIOUBL 2.1 phased out by 15 May 2026.

countries.name: Estonia

phases.applies_to: Public sector, for procurement above EU thresholds
Suppliers, on request, where the buyer is registered as an e-invoice recipient in the commercial register

countries.notes: Not a blanket mandate. The Accounting Act amendment works on a buyer's-choice principle: registered recipients are entitled to an EN 16931 invoice by default, and parties may still agree another format. Frequently misreported as a universal B2B mandate.

countries.name: Spain

phases.applies_to: Invoices to public entities through FACe (Law 25/2013): Facturae, or EN 16931 in UBL or CII
Businesses and professionals with turnover above EUR 8 million: issue, send and receive e-invoices and report their status
All other businesses and professionals: issue, send and receive e-invoices

sources.title: Solución pública de facturación electrónica: plazos

countries.notes: Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) requires B2B e-invoicing; Real Decreto 238/2026 (BOE 31 March 2026, in force 20 April 2026) sets the rules, and the deadlines run from Orden HAC/1028/2026, published in the BOE on 5 October 2026 and in force on 6 October 2026. Per the AEAT: businesses and professionals above EUR 8 million turnover must issue, send and receive e-invoices and report their status by 6 October 2027; all others by 6 October 2028, with status reporting for individuals by 6 October 2029. Invoices must follow EN 16931 in UBL, CII, EDIFACT or Facturae, exchanged via private platforms or the AEAT's free public solution (UBL). The 2025-2027 dates still in circulation are wrong. B2C is out of scope; VERI*FACTU and SII are separate regimes.

countries.name: Finland

phases.applies_to: Central government bodies, under the eInvoicing Act 241/2019
No mandate. Under Act 241/2019 businesses above EUR 10,000 turnover hold a right to request an EN 16931 invoice — an entitlement, not an obligation to use e-invoicing.

countries.notes: Finland's B2G scope goes beyond the Directive minimum to national thresholds.

countries.name: France

phases.applies_to: Invoices to the public sector through Chorus Pro (suppliers phased in from 2017 to 2020)
All VAT-taxable businesses established in France must be able to receive e-invoices
Large and mid-size companies (ETI) issue e-invoices and e-report
SMEs and micro-businesses issue e-invoices and e-report

sources.title: Tout savoir sur la facturation électronique pour les entreprises

countries.notes: Legal basis is CGI art. 289 bis, with the calendar set by the 2024 finance law as amended in 2026. Scope is VAT-taxable businesses established in France, including micro-entrepreneurs under the VAT franchise. Invoices are exchanged through approved platforms (plateformes agréées, formerly called PDP); the state runs no free public exchange portal but operates the central directory and the data concentrator. Sales to consumers and to businesses abroad are not e-invoiced but are covered by e-reporting on the same timetable. Fines: EUR 50 per invoice not issued electronically (capped at EUR 15,000 a year) and EUR 500 per missing e-reporting transmission. DGFiP became the Peppol authority for France in July 2025. B2G e-invoicing through Chorus Pro was phased in from 1 January 2017 (large companies) to 1 January 2020 (micro-enterprises).

countries.name: Greece

phases.applies_to: Gradual rollout across general government
General government expenditure above EUR 2,500
No B2B mandate; legislative amendments would be required and no date is set.

countries.notes: myDATA real-time VAT reporting is a separate regime and is not an e-invoicing mandate. KE.D is the central receiving point over Peppol.

countries.name: Croatia

phases.applies_to: All public-sector suppliers (Act on eInvoicing in Public Procurement, OJ 94/2018)
Businesses in the VAT system established in Croatia: issue and receive domestic B2B eRačun
Entities outside the VAT system — receiving only
Entities outside the VAT system and the public sector — issuing
EU-wide (ViDA): e-invoicing for intra-EU B2B transactions

sources.title: Izdavanje i primanje eRačuna i fiskalizacija eRačuna (FAQ, updated 30.1.2026)

countries.notes: Zakon o fiskalizaciji (Fiscalisation 2.0) was published in Narodne novine 89/25, entered into force on 1 September 2025 and applies from 1 January 2026. Note the split for entities outside the VAT system: they must receive from 1 January 2026 but only issue from 1 January 2027. Scope is businesses established in Croatia, for domestic B2B; foreign businesses with only a Croatian VAT number are out of scope, and eRačun does not cover B2C. Every eRačun must follow EN 16931 with the Croatian extension (HR CIUS) and carry a KPD classification code on each line, so a plain PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 invoice is not valid. Exchange runs through registered information intermediaries and the AMS address directory, and both issuer and recipient fiscalise each eRačun. MIKROeRAČUN is the free tool for non-VAT payers. The 2030 phase is the EU-wide ViDA intra-EU obligation, not national law.

countries.name: Hungary

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, for procurement above EU thresholds
Electricity and natural gas suppliers only
No general B2B e-invoicing mandate.

countries.notes: Hungary is routinely miscategorised. RTIR/NAV real-time invoice reporting (universal since 4 January 2021) is a VAT reporting obligation, not an e-invoicing mandate — any format the tax authority accepts may be used. The only sectoral e-invoicing obligation covers energy suppliers.

countries.name: Ireland

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, under Statutory Instrument 258/2019
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Any future obligation is expected via ViDA rather than domestic law.

countries.name: Italy

phases.applies_to: All suppliers to public administrations, via SdI
All VAT-registered Italian businesses, for domestic transactions

countries.notes: The EU's first universal B2B clearance mandate. The turnover-based exclusion for small businesses was removed in January 2024. Exchange is exclusively via the Sistema di Interscambio, not Peppol; Italy's derogation to keep SdI runs to 31 December 2027 under EU Decision 2024/3150.

countries.name: Lithuania

phases.applies_to: All suppliers in public procurement
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: SABIS replaced eSąskaita in September 2024 and is now the only accepted route, connected to Peppol.

countries.name: Luxembourg

phases.applies_to: Large companies
Medium-sized companies
Small and newly established businesses
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Phased B2G rollout by company size, complete since March 2023. Peppol is the backbone.

countries.name: Latvia

phases.applies_to: Suppliers to budget institutions (contracts concluded before 31 December 2024 may defer to 1 January 2026)
All businesses registered in Latvia

sources.title: Grozījumi Grāmatvedības likumā — obligātie e-rēķini no 2028. gada
Saeima adopts amendments to the Accounting Law (5 June 2025)

countries.notes: The Saeima adopted amendments to the Accounting Law (Grāmatvedības likums) as urgent on 5 June 2025, deferring the B2B obligation from 2026 to 1 January 2028. Many sources still quote 2026. B2G has applied since 1 January 2025; structured e-invoicing is voluntary for non-budget entities in the interim. Exemptions cover businesses using electronic tax registration devices, National Health Service systems, and national security agencies.

countries.name: Malta

phases.applies_to: Central contracting authorities and local councils, under Legal Notices 403/404 of 2018
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: No dedicated national e-invoicing platform. B2B/B2G expansion is under study in line with ViDA.

countries.name: Netherlands

phases.applies_to: Central government entities must receive and process EN 16931 invoices
Planned: e-invoicing between businesses, domestic and intra-EU (KOR businesses exempt); bill not yet passed

sources.title: Kabinet kiest voor invoering e-facturatie en rapportage voor bedrijven (11 September 2026)

countries.notes: On 11 September 2026 the cabinet chose to make B2B e-invoicing mandatory from 1 July 2030, with digital reporting from 1 July 2031; businesses under the small-business scheme (KOR) are exempt. The bill has not yet passed parliament, so the 2030 phase is provisional. Until then B2B e-invoicing is voluntary and requires the buyer's consent. Suppliers to central government must already send e-invoices; PEPPOL is one route, not the only one.

countries.name: Norway

phases.applies_to: Public-sector suppliers, for transactions above NOK 100,000 excluding VAT
Bookkeeping-obliged businesses must send e-invoices to bookkeeping-obliged buyers registered in ELMA
Bookkeeping-obliged businesses must keep digital accounts and receive e-invoices automatically

sources.title: Lov 19. juni 2026 nr. 39 om endringer i bokføringsloven (pliktig digital bokføring og e-fakturering mv.)
Nye lovregler om e-fakturering i næringslivet settes i kraft

countries.notes: EEA, not EU. Prop. 44 L (2025-2026) was passed by the Storting on 8 June 2026 and promulgated as Lov 2026-06-19-39; the Bookkeeping Act changes commence 1 January 2027 (sending) and 1 January 2030 (digital bookkeeping and automatic receipt). Scope is businesses with bookkeeping obligations (bokføringspliktige), not VAT registration. Until 2030 the sending duty applies only when the buyer is bookkeeping-obliged and registered as a receiver in ELMA (or another approved PEPPOL register); for such buyers a PDF does not suffice. Businesses with turnover up to NOK 50,000 a year only have to send e-invoices if their invoicing system can. From 1 January 2028 the buyer's organisation number must appear on the sales document. Formats are EHF / PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0; businesses are addressed by organisation number (ICD 0192). The obligation was pulled forward a year from 2028 by a government instruction of 16 March 2026. The Commission factsheet still records Norway as having no B2B mandate and is out of date.

countries.name: Poland

phases.applies_to: Contracting authorities, contracts of EUR 30,000 or more (PEF platform, Peppol)
All contracting authorities
All Polish VAT taxpayers must receive invoices through KSeF
Taxpayers whose 2024 sales including VAT exceeded PLN 200 million
All other taxpayers (sellers with invoiced sales up to PLN 10,000 gross a month may issue outside KSeF until 31 December 2026)
Taxpayers with invoiced sales up to PLN 10,000 gross a month; penalties for not using KSeF apply from this date

countries.notes: Two distinct regimes: B2G runs on Peppol via the PEF platform, while B2B uses the national KSeF clearance platform (KSeF 2.0, FA(3) structure, from 1 February 2026). The rollout was postponed from July 2024. Receiving through KSeF has been mandatory for every taxpayer since 1 February 2026; issuing on 1 February 2026 only above PLN 200 million (2024 sales including VAT), on 1 April 2026 for everyone else, and for sellers with invoiced sales up to PLN 10,000 gross a month on 1 January 2027. Penalties (up to 100% of the VAT on the invoice, or 18.7% of the gross amount) apply from 1 January 2027. The obligation follows the seller: Polish taxpayers also issue intra-EU supply, export and service invoices in KSeF and give foreign buyers a visualisation with a QR code. Foreign businesses without a seat or involved fixed establishment in Poland, B2C invoices and OSS/IOSS sales are out of scope.

countries.name: Portugal

phases.applies_to: Large companies (250+ employees, EUR 50M+ revenue or EUR 43M+ assets)
Small and medium-sized enterprises
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: Legal basis Lei n.º 111-B/2017 as amended. No B2B mandate: PDF invoices remain valid but from January 2026 require a Qualified Electronic Signature. SAF-T(PT) monthly reporting is a separate, long-standing regime.

countries.name: Romania

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, under Law 199/2020
Taxable persons established in Romania and non-established entities registered for Romanian VAT
All domestic B2C transactions taxable in Romania

countries.notes: One of the few member states with a B2C mandate as well as B2B. Invoices must reach RO e-Factura within five calendar days of issuance. National specification RO_CIUS under Order 1366/2021.

countries.name: Sweden

phases.applies_to: Public sector entities, under Act 2018:1277
No mandate; voluntary and subject to mutual agreement

countries.notes: No B2B mandate and no VAT real-time reporting. Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is used as the national CIUS without modification; voluntary adoption is high.

countries.name: Slovenia

phases.applies_to: All B2G and G2G transactions via the Public Payments Administration
All entities in the Business Register and natural persons performing an activity

sources.title: Zakon o izmenjavi elektronskih računov in drugih elektronskih dokumentov (ZIERDED), Uradni list RS 85/2025

countries.notes: ZIERDED was adopted by the Državni zbor on 23 October 2025 and published in Uradni list RS 85/2025 on 6 November 2025 — it is law, not a draft, and the date is 1 January 2028 rather than the 2027 often quoted from earlier drafts. B2C and cross-border e-invoicing remain optional. The act transposes Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 (ViDA). Accepted formats are e-SLOG 2.0 or another established structured standard.

countries.name: Slovakia

phases.applies_to: Central and sub-central authorities, under Act No. 2015/2019
VAT payers established in Slovakia, for domestic supplies to businesses and legal entities (recipients include non-VAT payers); B2G is covered on the same date
Extension to cross-border intra-EU transactions

sources.title: Zákon č. 385/2025 Z. z., ktorým sa mení a dopĺňa zákon č. 222/2004 Z. z. o DPH
sources.publisher: Slov-Lex (Collection of Laws of the Slovak Republic)

countries.notes: Adopted by the National Council on 9 December 2025 as Act No. 385/2025 Z. z., amending the VAT Act (222/2004). Mandatory from 1 January 2027 for domestic B2B and B2G, with a voluntary phase running since May 2026 and delivery over Peppol. B2C is out of scope. Often still listed as B2G-only.
